newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian free market active as index drifts up.
newsitem.headline: Estonian free market active as index drifts up.

text.p: Shares on Estonia's over-the-counter free market remained active on Monday, outstripping business on the official list, and the Tallinn stock exchange index drifted slightly higher, dealers said.
The free list traded 10.3 million kroons of stock while the official list was at 9.7 million kroons.
The market index, which traces only the official list, rose by 0.04 percent to 105.33.
The most active stock on the free market was the Tallinn Department store, which turned over 3.6 million kroons and rose to close at 57.75 kroons from 56.50 kroons.
Union Bank was busiest on the official list, rising slightly to 23.50 kroons from 23.40 kroons on 2.9 million kroons trade.
Tallinna Pank had volume of 1.25 million kroons and it closed at 40.50 kroons versus 40.35 kroons.
Savings Bank was little moved, trading just 700,000 kroons and closing at 39.35 kroons versus 39.40, after it published nine-month results.
"The results were as expected and investors are waiting for excellent results next year," said Hansapank trader Tonu Pekk.
Savings Bank said its nine month net profit was 38.4 million kroons versus 27.8 million kroons for the whole of last year.
